content.value_statement: GPU visuals can fail when shader APIs, package versions, and application lifecycles do not align. This skill guides version-aware vgpu development, integration, performance measurement, and validation.
actual_capabilities: Guides installed-version discovery and documentation lookup through the project's local vgpu executable.
Routes shader effects, geometry, particles, and 3D rendering tasks to relevant vgpu documentation.
Provides React lifecycle, resource cleanup, device loss, and Three.js renderer ownership guidance.
Explains version-specific bindings, depth targets, resizing, and multi-pass scheduling constraints.
Guides GPU performance measurement, resource reuse, resolution budgets, and adaptive quality decisions.
Defines shader validation, deterministic readback checks, real-frame inspection, and accessibility fallback checks.
limitations: Contains guidance only; it does not bundle vgpu, shader assets, or executable implementation scripts.
Requires version-matched documentation because API hints describe a reviewed 0.4.1 baseline.
Cannot guarantee hardware compatibility, visual correctness, or frame rate without actual rendering and measurement.
Does not provide HTML layout, accessible controls, or an automatic WebGL fallback.

use_cases.title: Integrate a Shader Surface
use_cases.description: Add a vgpu canvas to a React application while preserving semantic controls, reduced motion, and safe resource cleanup.

use_cases.title: Develop a Visual Effect
use_cases.description: Find compatible examples and shape shader composition, material behavior, and interactions using the installed package's documentation.

use_cases.title: Investigate GPU Regressions
use_cases.description: Separate compilation, transfer, submission, and rendering costs, then validate targeted changes on representative devices.

prompt_templates.title: Check the Installed Version
prompt_templates.prompt: Identify this project's installed vgpu version using its manifest, lockfile, and local executable. Summarize relevant documentation without installing another version.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Shader Effect
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a subtle interactive vgpu shader effect using version-matched docs. Preserve scrolling and reduced motion. Report shader validation and visual checks.

prompt_templates.title: Integrate with React
prompt_templates.prompt: Integrate this vgpu surface into React. Handle resize, asynchronous setup, unmount, device loss, and fallback content. Preserve semantic DOM controls.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: manage rendering within an application lifecycle.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Multi-Pass Rendering
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this vgpu multi-pass rendering issue. Verify versioned APIs, use deterministic readback tests, measure GPU costs, and report hardware checks and remaining uncertainty.

output_examples.input: How should I prepare an existing vgpu project before changing a shader?
output: Check the owning workspace's manifest and lockfile, then confirm the installed version with the local executable.
Read matching shader workflow documentation and inspect compatible examples before changing bindings or imports.
Validate the shader and inspect real frames after the change; report any checks that were not performed.

output_examples.input: My React canvas keeps rendering after its component disappears. What should I review?
output: Stop the frame loop, remove observers and listeners, and dispose resources owned by the component during teardown.
Handle asynchronous initialization completing after unmount and avoid disposing a shared context borrowed from another owner.
Test repeated mount and unmount, hidden-tab resume, initialization failure, and device loss.

output_examples.input: Why does my multi-pass effect become expensive on a high-resolution screen?
output: Measure CPU submission, GPU passes, transfers, startup compilation, and memory separately.
Clamp effective pixel density and render-target dimensions, then compare quality on a representative device.
Reuse resources and avoid per-frame allocation or GPU readback; do not claim a frame-rate improvement without measurements.

best_practices: Use the installed executable and version-matched documentation before implementing API calls.
Keep essential controls and text in semantic DOM, with reduced-motion support and visible fallback content.
Validate shaders and inspect real frames, then report the visual and hardware checks actually performed.
anti_patterns: Using unpinned package runners or hosted examples without checking compatibility with the installed version.
Giving two independent render loops ownership of one canvas or disposing a context owned elsewhere.
Treating mock tests or a successful bundler build as proof of shader validity, rendering correctness, or GPU performance.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Running project commands requires appropriate local tool access.

faq.question: Does this skill install vgpu automatically?
faq.answer: It prioritizes installed executables. Dependency restoration is task-scoped, and documentation access may use an explicitly selected package version.

faq.question: Is this an official Vercel skill?
faq.answer: No. It is a community skill that credits upstream vgpu guidance and adds integration and visual direction.

faq.question: Does it provide a fallback for unsupported WebGPU?
faq.answer: No automatic WebGL fallback is provided. The guidance calls for a poster, CSS treatment, or simpler renderer when GPU initialization fails.

faq.question: Can it work with an existing Three.js scene?
faq.answer: It directs you to version-matched integration documentation. Three.js should retain ownership of its renderer, scene, bindings, and frame loop.

faq.question: Are mock tests enough to verify a shader?
faq.answer: No. Mock tests check API behavior, not hardware rendering or WGSL validity. Use shader validation, real-frame inspection, and representative device measurements.
